ὁπλότερος , α, ον, Comp. without any Posit. in use, Ep. for νεώτερος,
A.the younger, always of persons, Il. 4.325 , Od. 21.370 , B. 10.71 ; ὁπλότερος γενεῇ younger by birth, Il. 2.707 , Od. 19.184 : fem. gen. pl. “ὁπλοτεράων”
Il. 14.267
, 275 : Sup. , youngest,
“ὁπλότατος γενεῆφιν”
9.58
; “ὁ. θυγάτηρ”
Od. 7.58
, cf. 11.283 , Hes. Th. 946 , Pi. I. 6(5).6 , al. : Ar. Pax 1270 - 1 uses the Comp. in mock heroic lines.—The orig. sense was perh. capable of bearing arms; and so ὁπλότεροι would be the serviceable men, hence, the young men, opp. the old men and children, Il. 3.108 , Hom. Epigr. 4.5 ; then simply, younger or youngest, hence of women, “Νέστορος ὁπλοτάτη θυγάτηρ”
Od. 3.465
, etc. ; then, as the youngest are the last born, ἄνδρες ὁπλότεροι also means the latter generations, men of later days,
Theoc. 16.46 ; “ὁπλοτέρου τ᾽ Ἀχιλῆος ἀκούομεν Εὐρυλόχοιο”
Euph. 80
.
From A Greek-English Lexicon (Henry George Liddell, Robert Scott, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1940)
